title: Beyond Blind Noising: Disentangled Visual Rectification for Hallucination Mitigation in MLLMs
claim: Under input perturbation, one encoder's features drift systematically toward spurious semantic directions while another's stay orthogonal, revealing distinct failure mechanisms.
layout: single line plot, two series with shaded bands, inset stats box
description: A single line chart titled 'Hallucination Subspace Projection (Averaged over Multiple Concept Pairs)'. The x-axis is noise intensity σ from 0 to 1.0. The y-axis is average projection score from -0.10 to 0.30. A red line with circle markers (CLIP) rises sharply around σ≈0.3 and then plateaus near 0.20. It has a wide pink shaded standard-deviation band. A blue line with square markers (DINOv3) hovers around zero and fluctuates slightly within a narrow light-blue band. A grey dashed horizontal line marks the random baseline at 0. A legend sits at top left. A yellow rounded box at top right lists the values at σ=1.0: CLIP 0.1988 ± 0.0519, DINO 0.0011 ± 0.0204, Δ = 0.1977. The eye goes first to the red curve diverging from the flat blue one.
caption: Geometric Analysis of Noise-Induced Feature Drift. We project the visual feature drift vector ∆z onto a pre-defined semantic hallucination direction vh (e.g., Dining Table →Vase) across varying noise intensities σ. Shaded regions denote standard deviation across multiple concept pairs. (Red) CLIP exhibits significant positive correlation (S ≈0.20 at σ = 1.0), confirming that noise triggers directional drift toward linguistic priors (hallucination induction). (Blue) In contrast, DINOv3 maintains near-zero projection (S ≈0.00), demonstrating that its feature degradation remains orthogonal to semantic hallucination directions, reflecting pure structural information loss. Detailed experimental settings are provided in Appendix A.
abstract: Visual Contrastive Decoding (VCD) mitigates hallucinations in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) by penalizing the output shift from noise-perturbed images, assuming this shift captures the hallucination direction. We prove this assumption flawed: noise-induced drift in Language-Image Pretrained (LIP) encoders is a \emph{coupled vector} entangling (i) structural degradation from corrupted visual information with (ii) hallucination induction from linguistic prior activation. VCD's indiscriminate penalty inevitably suppresses valid visual semantics. Our key insight is that Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) encoders exhibit \emph{only} structural degradation under noise—geometrically orthogonal to hallucination paths—enabling principled disentanglement via LIP--SSL differential response. We propose \textbf{Disentangled Visual Rectification (DVR)}, a training-free dual-stream framework performing visual-layer rectification and decoding-layer contrast on purified representations. DVR achieves approximately $5\times$ theoretical error reduction over VCD and establishes SOTA performance on POPE, MME, LLaVA-Bench and CHAIR benchmarks.
